instructions: Datumesh: every answer is a signed receipt. This mesh holds finance (exchange rates from the ECB, yields from the US Treasury, interest rates from the ECB and the Bank of England), scripture (texts, provenance), earth (monthly rainfall computed from CHIRPS) and registry (licences). Ask find in plain words for what you need. Use find to discover names, by words, a name, a label or a value of the lists above. Use get for a cell: a call (name(arg: value, ...)) or a cell:// URI, or a plain reference (a label and a reference, such as "<label> <reference>") that the mesh resolves and reads in the same call. For a text value, get gives its text, checked. Use explain for its lineage and verify for a receipt; verify with text checks a quoted text against the cell's text after NFC. define and publish write under this machine's unrooted namespace.

tools.description: Names held here whose name contains the query (case-insensitive). When none are held, or with remote, also the configured find_meshes (and the forward mesh with remote); searched lists each place looked and its status. A class is followed by its methods.
tools.name: find

tools.description: The answer to a call (name(arg: value, ...)) or a cell:// URI, as a signed receipt. A text blob's content (up to 64 KiB) comes first, checked against its SHA-256 (blob_checked); otherwise its blob:// address and size. A slice of more than 100 members answers a summary (count, first and last key, and for numbers min, max and mean), its first 100 members and the calc call that aggregates the slice (mean for numbers, else count): run that calc to get the aggregate. A plain reference (a label and a reference, such as "<label> <reference>") is read through the mesh's find in the same call: an exact one gives its answer, an ambiguous one its candidates, a range is refused (E_RANGE_REFUSED), and a reference nothing resolves to gives suggestions.
tools.name: get

tools.description: The lineage of a cell: its answer and the answers of its inputs, to depth.
tools.name: explain

tools.description: A class, object, cell or short id (SPEC 16.8), as the mesh describes it.
tools.name: describe

tools.description: Verifies a receipt (its JSON) with this machine's keys.
tools.name: verify

tools.description: Defines a function under local/ (a formula with its signature, or a stored function with its signature) or a class (its descriptor). A formula may come with its tests, in the same call: each names the function as its call, with its expect (a plain literal typed by the return type, or {"fault": code}) and optionally asof and inputs. Tests are optional here, and a stored function takes none; a publish to a public mesh needs them (publish_public).
tools.name: define

tools.description: Publishes publish-stored lines under local/ (functions, classes and cells), each cell signed by this machine.
tools.name: publish

tools.description: The spreadsheet what-if (also called a diddle or a tweak, for those who know SecDB-style systems): the value a cell would have if some cells held other values, or the value of one cell that makes another equal a number (solve). The answer is a labelled scenario, never signed or stored, and never a fact: it has no receipt and is not verified. Nothing else changes.
tools.name: whatif

tools.description: Calculate here, not in code: the formula runs beside the data and returns only the result, with its lineage (the cells it read). Try find for an existing function first. The result is memoised on this machine, so the same calculation is not run twice; with remote it is scoped on the forward mesh and nothing is kept.
tools.name: calc

tools.description: The forward mesh's members of a function over a range of keys (x_interval), each with its receipt, resolving aliases. Keys may be omitted for an unkeyed series. Over 100 members it answers a summary (count, first and last keys, min, max and mean for numbers), the first 100 members, and the interval call for the rest.
tools.name: interval

tools.description: Publishes a rooted namespace of this machine's names to a public mesh (the bundle, with its tests). Each formula needs tests that cover its derived cases and every branch (E_TESTS_MISSING lists what is missing); the mesh checks the rest and refuses with its code.
tools.name: publish_public
